mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.15% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing statistically significant positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the market prices in accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods where FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.15% (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline return distribution).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as risk-off sentiment dominates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of triggered instances (UNRATE rise >0.3pp).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate contractionary supply shocks, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns through reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >40% of periods where INDPRO falls >1.5% and PAYEMS falls >0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, housing starts (HOUST) below 1,100 thousand units signal weakening consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 20-day returns as real estate sector weakness spreads.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of late-cycle periods with HOUST < 1,100.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS) growth exceeding 0.8% monthly signals robust consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns through sustained corporate revenue momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >35% of RSAFS growth >0.8% monthly periods.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 235.0 (CPIAUCSL) triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 5-day returns as bond yields rise and equity multiples contract.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >45% of CPIAUCSL >235.0 periods.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 104.0 indicates manufacturing slowdown, producing negative S&P 500 20-day returns as supply chain disruptions reduce corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of INDPRO < 104.0 periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate above 5.5% and payrolls decline exceeding 0.5% (PAYEMS) signals labor market weakness, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns through reduced consumer spending power.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >40% of periods where UNRATE >5.5% and PAYEMS falls >0.5%.
